issue_context.title: VoxelGI, ReflectionProbe FogVolume Extents should be replaced with Size for consistency with CSGBox3D
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.dev (6b0b1a4c0)

### System information

Fedora 34, GeForce GTX 1080 (NVIDIA 470.74)

### Issue description

With https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/44183, we started moving from Extents properties to Size properties. This Size property is the same as extents, but with all values halved (which means the values you need to specify are twice as large to obtain the same size as before).

To ensure consistency within the Godot API, we should finish this compatibility breaking change before 4.0 is released.

### Steps to reproduce

- Add a VoxelGI, ReflectionProbe or FogVolume node.
- Notice how the size is still defined using an half-extents property rather than a size like CSGBox3D is.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments: In many cases 'extents' properties are set to default values such as Vector3(1, 1, 1). Do we want to maintain this size (as in change the default to Vector3(2, 2, 2)) or should the defaults be retained and just start out smaller?

> In many cases 'extents' properties are set to default values such as Vector3(1, 1, 1). Do we want to maintain this size (as in change the default to Vector3(2, 2, 2)) or should the defaults be retained and just start out smaller?

I think we can revise the values to be larger if they are typically used at larger sizes. For instance, [the default extents of a ReflectionProbe were increased in `master`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/49953) to make them easier to see when you add one to the scene.

That makes sense, thanks - if I have a go at doing this I'll retain default values of (0,0,0), check the usage for values of (1,1,1), and assume other values to be intentionally sized and double them as necessary.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66553618/140776163-3ac48465-0173-4106-951c-b43a74fe5097.png)
I'm afraid I need advice on this line in `renderer_scene_render_rd.cpp`, as I'm having trouble understanding it. Surely width/height/depth should have been divided by 2 here to result in `extents`, since width means the full width of an object and so a subset of its size? Should I multiply them by 2 to compensate, ignore it, or edit interactions with `VolumetricFog` so that it works on a different size scale?

Edit: nevermind, I had to go for a moment but looking back at it I've realised this refers to the extents of `VolumetricFog`, which will obviously be different from `FogVolume` anyway. I assume that `VolumetricFog` can continue to use `extents` as normal (isn't included in this issue).

review_comments: Note that `p_half_extents` was actually named wrong before. The `extents` (unchanged) were always passed in, which is half the size.
I'm skeptical about this. This effectively decreases the minimum size by half

Yeah that was my thought as well.

EDIT: Just checked, can confirm the minimum size is halfed now. Doesn't make any problems though:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66004280/214974732-8fdbe31b-38d4-4356-ba0f-6891c745954a.png)
Okay, should be fine. If I recall correctly the minimum size was chosen rather arbitrarily
